extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal education funds (K-12 and postsecondary administrators, Title IX coordinators, campus legal counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for institutions' Title IX grievance procedures, including standards of proof, procedural safeguards, notice and appeal obligations, and anti-bias/training requirements. Focused on how recipients must structure and operate investigative and adjudicative processes for sex discrimination complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of standard of proof (preponderance or clear and convincing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may use either the preponderance of the evidence standard or the clear and convincing evidence standard to determine whether sex discrimination occurred, provided the standard selected for allegations of sex discrimination is not higher than the standard selected for other types of discrimination or comparable offenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department expresses view that preponderance best promotes Title IX compliance (encourages reporting, addresses discrimination), but allows recipient flexibility. The beyond a reasonable doubt standard is never appropriate. The Department notes concerns about the vagueness of clear and convincing and recommends recipients consider the implications of their choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparable proceedings must use same or higher (not lower) standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure the standard chosen for sex discrimination is not higher than the standard used in other comparable proceedings (e.g., other discrimination complaints involving the same category of respondents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a recipient uses clear and convincing for some comparable proceedings and preponderance for others, it must use preponderance for sex discrimination. The Department declined to rigidly define 'comparable proceedings,' leaving reasonable determinations to recipients, but states comparability generally includes similar person-to-person physical offenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker evaluation limited to evidence that is relevant and not otherwise impermissible
rubrics_metrics.description: Under either standard of proof, the evidence the decisionmaker evaluates must be both 'relevant' and 'not otherwise impermissible.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'and not otherwise impermissible' was added to §106.45(h)(1) for clarity and consistency; decisionmakers should exclude evidence the regulations prohibit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must treat complainants and respondents equitably
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must 'treat complainants and respondents equitably' as required by §106.45(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable treatment is a core requirement; inequitable procedural rights (e.g., giving panel-challenge rights to employees but not students) can violate Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissive dismissal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have discretion to dismiss a complaint in the four circumstances listed in §106.45(d)(1)(i)-(iv), including when the allegations, even if proven, would not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissive dismissal can prevent baseless proceedings from proceeding; grievance procedures must document dismissal bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to parties of the allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide notice to the parties of the allegations as required by §106.45(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice is central to due process and to parties' ability to respond and prepare for proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow procedures before imposing disciplinary sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures 'must be followed before the imposition of any disciplinary sanctions against a respondent' (§106.45(h)(4)), and sanctions may be imposed only if it is determined the respondent engaged in prohibited sex discrimination (§106.45(h)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients cannot bypass the established grievance process when seeking to discipline respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of all relevant evidence and exclusion of impermissible evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide an 'objective evaluation of all relevant evidence' and must exclude certain types of evidence as impermissible (§106.45(b)(6) and (7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective evaluation requires avoiding bias and applying evidence rules consistently; prohibited evidence types must be identified and excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden on recipient to gather sufficient evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden is on the recipient to conduct an investigation that gathers sufficient evidence to reach a determination (§106.45(f)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This places investigative responsibility with the institution, not with the complainant or respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to present witnesses and relevant evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must 'provide an equal opportunity for the parties to present fact witnesses and other inculpatory and exculpatory evidence that are relevant and not otherwise impermissible' (§106.45(f)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both parties should have comparable chances to present information that bears on the allegations; relevance and permissibility limits apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal access to evidence and chance to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party must be provided 'an equal opportunity to access the evidence that is relevant and not otherwise impermissible and a reasonable opportunity to respond to that evidence' (§106.45(f)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and evidence sharing procedures must be symmetric; recipients should provide adaptive formats as needed for disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker must adequately assess credibility when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: The decisionmaker must 'adequately assess a party's or witness's credibility to the extent credibility is in dispute and relevant to the allegations' (§106.45(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credibility determinations must be grounded in the evidence and explained in the rationale where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker impartiality and conflict-of-interest prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisionmakers 'not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual complainant or respondent' (§106.45(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure panels and adjudicators are neutral; policies should include procedures to identify and remedy conflicts or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of non-responsibility until determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must include a presumption that 'the respondent is not responsible for the alleged conduct until a determination whether sex discrimination occurred is made' (§106.45(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption is a required protection and should be reflected in written procedures and trainings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections for parties and witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must 'take reasonable steps to protect the privacy of the parties and witnesses during the grievance procedures' (§106.45(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy measures should balance transparency for process fairness with confidentiality needs; training should cover privacy safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements for decisionmakers (avoid prejudgment and bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.8(d) requires training for decisionmakers, including on serving impartially by avoiding prejudgment of the facts at issue, conflicts of interest, and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must address implicit bias, prejudgment, conflict-of-interest identification, and proper evidence assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals requirement and minimum parity
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45(i) requires a recipient to offer parties an appeal that, at minimum, is the same as it offers in all other comparable proceedings; §106.45(d)(3) provides the right to appeal dismissal of a complaint; §106.46(i) requires postsecondary institutions to offer appeals on bases such as procedural irregularity or bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must be available consistently across comparable proceedings and may be offered on additional equal bases; appeal procedures should be in writing and accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notification of determination and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.45(h)(2) requires recipients to provide written notification to both complainant and respondent of the determination whether sex discrimination occurred and a rationale for that determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written notice facilitates transparency and appeals, should be provided in adaptive formats as necessary for disabilities, and assists parents/guardians; recordkeeping obligations under §106.8(f)(1) support this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change 'should not' to 'must not' in determining discrimination when not persuaded
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department revised the second sentence of §106.45(h)(1) to replace 'should not' with 'must not' to make clear that a recipient may not determine sex discrimination occurred if the decisionmaker is not persuaded by the available evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversely, if the decisionmaker is persuaded under the applicable standard, they must determine that sex discrimination occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may use different standards for students and employees (flexibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are afforded flexibility to use a different standard of proof for student conduct than for employee conduct, recognizing differing obligations (e.g., collective bargaining agreements, state laws) regarding employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must publish grievance procedures in writing and state which standard of proof they will use (§106.45(a)(1) and (h)(1)). The Department defends flexibility while cautioning about perceptions of fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on tiered/sliding-scale standards based on sanctions or allegation type
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department rejects a sliding scale or tiered approach (e.g., varying standard based on potential sanctions or type of allegation) as impracticable and likely to create unpredictability and inequity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should not attempt to set different standards depending on potential sanctions or allegation severity because of administrative difficulty and fairness concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to consider other Title IX duties even if standard not met
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when evidence does not meet the chosen standard of proof, recipients must consider whether they have other obligations under the regulations to take prompt and effective steps to ensure sex discrimination does not continue or recur (e.g., non-disciplinary steps under §106.44(f)(1)(vii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should document consideration of remedies and non-disciplinary measures even when no determination of sex discrimination is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid singling out sex-based harassment by using a higher standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not use a higher standard of proof for sex discrimination than they use for comparable offenses because that would impermissibly discriminate based on sex and 'reinforce harmful myths about the credibility of sex discrimination complainants.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure parity across types of discrimination; raising standards for sex complaints while keeping lower standards elsewhere would violate the rule's non-discrimination intent.
